items.title: Billy Taylor interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995
items.q: His early career included work with some of the best soloists in jazz, including ... Machito

ctx.x: Dr. Billy Taylor continues to be this country’s most articulate and informed spokesman for American jazz. His unique perspective as a pianist, composer, educator and media figure have made him much in demand since his first gigs in New York in the early 1940’s. He was born in North Carolina in 1921 and completed his Bachelor of Music degree from Virginia State College in 1942.

His early career included work with some of the best soloists in jazz, including Dizzy Gillespie, Ben Webster, Cozy Cole and Machito, who inspired an avid interest in Latin music. He led his own trio during the 50’s and 60’s and later became the first black musical director on television, leading the band for the David Frost Show from 1969-72. Taylor is a prolific composer, his best known work, “I Wish I Knew How it Feels to be Free” has been recorded numerous times, both instrumentally and as a vocal piece.
